subject: Clarifying tombstone, purge timeline, and default retention behavior
messages:
From: Lucy Chen <lucy@acmehealth.com>

Date: Sat, 16 May 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question on deletion/tombstone behavior

Hi Hannah,

We're evaluating Redwood for a PHI-adjacent use case and have one implementation question before the legal review. If a customer requests data deletion (or triggers a purge via the console), does Redwood immediately 'tombstone' or mark records as deleted and then run a background purge? How long does data remain in a recoverable/quarantine state after a deletion request?

Specifics we'd like clarified:
- Default retention for hosted API request/response logs (prompts and generated outputs) vs. derivative artifacts (embeddings, traces).
- Whether prompts or model outputs are considered distinct "artifacts" for retention accounting.
- Can customers trigger an immediate hard-delete (and how long until physical purge)?

Attaching a small schema of the kinds of fields we send (sample-data-schema.csv). Happy to hop on a short call.

Thanks,
Lucy
Sr. IT Security Analyst | Acme Health

Hi Lucy — thanks for the clear note. Short answer: we use a two-stage deletion process (soft-delete/tombstone then scheduled physical purge) for hosted deployments, and we can accelerate purges for enterprise customers by request. I've looped in Marissa (product) and Karthik (security) to provide the exact timelines and examples that map to your use case.

I'll also attach our SOC2 FAQ which covers audit trail behavior. Can you confirm whether Acme would require a contractual accelerated purge SLA (24–72h) or if a standard support-initiated purge is sufficient? If you want an attestation, legal can prepare one after we confirm timelines.

Subject: Re: Quick question on deletion/tombstone behavior — details and examples

Hi Lucy / Hannah — jumping in with concrete detail so you can map this to your security review. High level first, then examples.

High-level policy (hosted Redwood API):
- Default capture: By default, for hosted API customers, request metadata and request/response payloads (prompts and generated outputs) are retained to support debugging, quality monitoring, and abuse detection. The standard retention window is 30 days from ingestion.
- Tombstone / soft-delete: When a deletion is requested by a customer (via the Console deletion workflow or Support DSR), we immediately mark affected records as tombstoned: accessible only to internal compliance workflows, not returned to APIs or UI queries. Tombstoned records remain in a quarantined state for up to 90 days to support audit requests, retention-consistent backups, and forensics.
- Hard-delete / physical purge: After the quarantine period we run background jobs that purge data from primary stores and eventually from longer-term backups. Physical purge completion is typically within 90–180 days depending on backend storage tier; for many customers the effective hard-delete occurs ~90 days after tombstone.
- Accelerated purge for enterprise: For enterprise contracts (and for Acme under an accelerated-purge addendum), we offer an expedited purge path — upon verified request we can complete physical deletion within 24–72 hours. This requires an attestation and a ticket tracked by our Security team.

What counts as "logs" vs "artifacts":
- Prompts & outputs: Both prompts (customer-provided text) and generated outputs (model responses) are treated as stored artifacts when capture is enabled. They are included in the 30-day default retention window for hosted customers.
- Derivative artifacts: embeddings, evaluation traces, and model telemetry are stored under separate buckets with their own TTLs; embeddings default to 90 days unless the customer has configured long-term storage.
- Ephemeral items: KV cache entries and live streaming buffers are ephemeral and are not written to the long-term log store unless the customer explicitly uses storage APIs (e.g., save to dataset).

Customer-triggered deletion workflow (example steps):
1) Customer opens DSR via Console or Support (we create ticket ACME-DSR-###).
2) Records are tombstoned immediately (no longer accessible via any customer-facing endpoints).
3) Security validates scope and sends confirmation to customer (within 48 hours).
4) Physical purge scheduled (standard 90-day quarantine); if accelerated purge requested and contracted, Security triggers expedited pipeline (24–72h).

Notes & caveats:
- Private deployments (VPC / on-prem): Redwood's control plane does not pull or retain customer payloads by default. All retention/purge is customer-controlled in their environment. Our guidance and scripts can be used to run secure wipes if required.
- Backups and cold storage: Backups are rotated according to our backup retention policies; deletion from backups may take longer. We maintain an internal audit log of deletion actions for compliance.
- Auditability: Tombstone markers and deletion events are logged with an audit record (who requested, scope, ticket ID). This audit record is kept for compliance and is typically not subject to the same purge schedules as payload data.

If helpful, I can provide a short table mapping artifact types to default TTLs for your review. Otherwise we can schedule a 30-minute call to walk Acme's legal and security through the attestation flow.

— Karthik
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
